  "reasoning": "All 16 selected answers agree with their own captured worked solutions and are mathematically correct. There are authored errors in the explanations: q-49354 changes the denominator from x+2 to x+5 in one displayed integral, although its decomposition and final answer correctly use x+2. In q-2751 and q-79342, the source incorrectly says the derivatives are undefined at the endpoints; the displayed functions have derivatives there. Endpoints are extrema candidates regardless of whether they are interior critical points. These errors do not change the answers.\n\nFor q-77888, only h is continuous on [-1,3] and differentiable on (-1,3). The other graphs have a discontinuity, an interior corner, or an endpoint asymptote. For q-48399, f's discontinuity at -1 is outside [0,2], and its graph is smooth throughout (0,2); the other choices fail continuity or differentiability. For q-127013, II and III have their corners at endpoints, while I has an interior corner. For q-125262, I and III are smooth everywhere; ln(x) is undefined at 0.\n\nFor q-12497, u=3x+1 produces (1/9)∫(u^(3/2)-u^(1/2))du. For q-2621, u=4-x produces -∫(9u^(1/2)-2u^(3/2))du. For q-49529, x=(u+1)/2 and dx=du/2, with bounds 1 and 5, give the factor 1/4. For q-17045, u=2-x gives ∫₀²(2-u)u^(3/2)du=32√2/35=√(2^11)/35.\n\nThe rational integrands in q-49354, q-49456, and q-73392 decompose respectively as 5-3/(x+2), 3x²+1+2/(x-3), and 1/2-2/(x+3), yielding the stated antiderivatives. For q-114898, the integrand is 2+3/(4x-1); evaluating 2x+(3/4)ln|4x-1| gives [1-3ln(3/2)]/4.\n\nFor q-4798, reversing and scaling the given integral gives ∫₃⁶f=5, so ∫₀⁶f=3+5=8. For q-114019, ∫₋₁¹f=1 and the odd term -6x integrates to zero. For q-2751, √x increases, so its maximum is √9=3. For q-79342, the endpoint and stationary-point values at -1,0,2,3 are 3,-1,3,-1, so the minimum is -1. There is no earlier submitted answer or revealed grade to reconcile.",
